MEMORANDUM FOR SUBJECT DATE ARACELI A. SAN JOSE, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG Regional Office III REQUEST FOR GUIDANCE ON THE EXECUTIVE ORDER 1, SERIES OF 2025 ISSUED BY THE GOVERNOR OF TARLAC CONCERNING THE ROAD CLOSURE IN THE CITY OF TARLAC [R03-ORD-2025-03-12-0041 JUL 3 1 2025 Reference: Memorandum dated March 7, 2025, from DILG Region Ill, requesting for this level's legal opinion on the validity of Executive Order (EO) No. 1 Series of 2025 issued by the Govemor of Tarlac. EO No. 1, Series of 2025 issued by the Governor Susan S. Yap mandates the temporary closure of certain roads and streets in light of the forthcoming Kanlahi Festival, a province-wide event. However, the roads and streets subject of such closure are under the ownership and jurisdiction of the City Government of Tarlac. Relative thereto, you seek clarification on the following: 1. Which LGU has the power to temporarily close the city roads within the territorial jurisdiction of a component city, such as Tarlac City in connection with a cultural celebration? Is it the Tarlac City or the Province of Tarlac? 2. What are the requisites for temporary closure of national and city roads within the territorial jurisdiction of a component city, such as Tarlac City? 3. Who is the "concerned local chief executive" empowered to temporarily close national and city roads within the territorial jurisdiction of component Tarlac City for the Kanlahi Festival? Is it the City Mayor of the component Tarlac City or the Provincial Governor? Since your first and second query are interrelated, we shall jointly discuss the same. Foremost, we concur with your view that it is the City Government of Tarlac that possesses the authority to temporarily close the city roads and streets, as it falls within its territorial jurisdiction. The manner of closure and opening of roads, whether temporary or permanent, is provided under Section 21 of the Local Government Code of 1991, viz: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline 8876-34-54

Section 21. Closure and Opening of Roads. — (a) A local ovemment unit ma ursuant to an ordinance ermanentl or tem oraril close o en an local road allo ark ors uare fallin within its iurisdiction: Provided, however, that in case of permanent closure, such ordinance must be approved by at least two-thirds (2/3) of all the members of the sanggunian, and when necessary, an adequate substitute for the public facility that is subject to closure is provided. xxx xxx XXX (c) An national or local road alle ark or s uare ma be tem orari/ closed durinq an actual emergency, or fiesta celebrations, public ralliest agricultural or industrial fairs. or an undertaking of public works and hiqhways. telecommunications. and waterworks projects. the duration of which shall be specified bv the local chief executive concerned in a written order: Provided, however, That no national or local road, alley, park, or square shall be temporarily closed for athletic, cultural, or civic activities not officially sponsored, recognized, or approved by the local govemment unit concemed xxx xxx xxx From the aforequoted provisions, temporary and permanent closure and opening of roads and streets generally require the enactment of an ordinance by the Sanggunian of the local government unit concerned. Stated otherwise, local roads can only be temporarily closed through an ordinance passed by the Sanggunian. This ensures a legal basis for the action, promotes checks and balances between the executive and legislative branches, and provides transparency by requiring public consultation and formal deliberation. Be that as it may, while Tarlac City is a component city of the Province of Tarlac, nonetheless, it is local government — with a city mayor and a Sanggunian who has autonomous powers over its infrastructure, traffic management and including the right to impose a road closure well within its city limits. As to your third query, we answer in the affirmative. The City Mayor of Tarlac is empowered to regulate or close city roads for public purposes such as festivals or special events, pursuant to Section 21 of the LGC. Since the Kanlahi Festival is an event also celebrated within the city then the City Mayor as the primary local chief executive is responsible for issuing an ordinance for the closure of city roads during the festival — not the Provincial Governor This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities, and of the courts. We hope to have provided you sufficient guidance on the matter. ATTY. ROMEO . BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Page 2 of 2
